fixes: Make the split the subject: a real glazed partition at least 3 cm thick on a sill with a top rail, a reflection streak and the two cyan glows mirrored in it; carts pulled in back to back against the glass so the paired cyan is the centre of the frame.

Pull the camera in and lower about 10 degrees so the cutaway fills from dek to footer; pills on the front wall's top edge; doors with frames, recessed panel and lever; tile mortar depth; people pressing into seats.

Get rid of the type band: the top 37 percent is a flat blue wash with a hard edge. Pull back and tilt up so the wall itself runs to the top, seat the type with a light wash over real surface, pegboard tops end in a moulded rail with a shadow.

Turn the elevation into a three quarter view raked 25 to 35 degrees so front coils come up large and back ones recede, chest pieces show rims and depth, tubing drapes with weight. Keep the blue channel, fix the floating hook shadows, fill the empty board below the bottom row.
Make the room read as a simulation stage: a one-way observation mirror with a dim observer booth, a ceiling dome camera and a boom mic over the table, a blank role badge on the actor.

Stage a live conversation: the clinician faces the actor across the table edge, three quarter away, leaning in mid-gesture; the actor's shoulders turn toward the clinician; the page plainly face down with its edge tilted; desk out of the footer corner; floor a different saturated tone from the walls.

Model the rocker as a real thrown rocker: paddle tilted so the cyan off end stands proud and the top sinks into the bezel, gloss specular along the bend, a dark gap at the low end, a hard shadow from the proud lip.
Wider softer wood grain with real seams on the blue boards (not scanlines); the ribbon an opaque saturated woven silk falling out of the page block with a contact shadow.

Make the laptop the destination: full CH.toolMat cyan on the screen with spill on the rail's far cap and nearest ridges, ridges visibly tighter toward the laptop, a carriage pointer edge on the zero ridge.

Replace the speckled sand plane with the limestone desk slab with a weathered front edge, grain and indigo contact shadows; lower toward the 11 cm worm's eye so the rail rakes from bottom left; chamfer and wear the end cap and tabs; first tab clearly lit brass.

Drop the camera to about 25 degrees above the slab and push in so the two slips fill the frame from edge to edge. Run the slab out of the frame at the top instead of ending it at a hard horizon under a flat sky band. Make the slab real worn limestone, or a warm stone with a chipped front edge and visible grain, not a flat terracotta field. Give each slip a slight curl, paper tooth and a soft indigo contact shadow, so they read as paper on stone rather than face-on cards drawn like a UI. This also clears the empty orange middle band.

Remove the dark blue rounded wash behind the headline. At 432 px it reads as a type plate floating on the sky. Seat the type in quiet the picture itself makes, such as the out-of-focus back of the slab or a deep cerulean sweep that darkens toward the top, and hold it with CH.seat only as a gradient you can't see the edges of. On the interrogating slip, make the annotations a pencil or brass-ink tone and keep cyan for the pen tip alone, so the accent keeps its one meaning. The three brass tabs with the second lit match FIG.questions and stay.

Make the handoff direction the picture: turn the three rails so each ends at the tool, with a cyan-rimmed receiving pan (CH.toolMat) on the far side or rails running toward the laptop; shuttles stay parked on the clinician's side.

Finish the props: bevel brass frames, curled paper, contact shadows under shuttles and tabs; bigger numbered tabs in a brass base; crop or pose the soft hands; camera lower and closer; keep the far tray clear of the dek.

Make the paper belong in a clinic: rolls mounted horizontally on exam-paper dispensers with brackets and a tear bar, sheets draping across a real clinic counter with a glove box or sharps bin and a coiled stethoscope, crinkled paper texture, curl at the free end, indigo contact shadows.
Hands close on the paper corner pulling it taut; counter fills to the footer with a hard contact shadow; deepen the sky behind kicker and counter toward cerulean.

Bring the camera down and in on the front desk so the two closed laptops and the coiled stethoscope cover about a third of the frame, with the empty desk rows going soft behind them. Give the laptops real hinge and edge bevels, a satin aluminium lid in a saturated tone colour and a clear cyan sleep light on each, at equal intensity and big enough to read at 432 px.

Clear a quiet seat for the headline. Its last line is set over the back rows of red chairs and desk legs. Swing the camera so the plain blue back wall fills the upper right, or lower the back rows below the type block. Replace the grey carpet strip at left with the warm floor.

Round 1 fix 1 only half landed, so it carries over. What landed: the slips now curl, the contact shadows are soft and indigo, and the surface fades into haze with no hard horizon. What did not land: the camera is still low and far back, so the two slips fill only a thin strip at about 55 to 70 percent of the frame height, with an empty band of blurred haze between the dek and the slips. The slab also reads as banded pale wood or sand, not limestone, and has no chipped edge. Raise the camera to about 25 degrees and push in until the slips fill the width and at least the lower half of the frame, with the surface running up behind the dek. Give the slab real limestone: fossil flecks, uneven pores, soft tone shifts and a visible worn, chipped front edge in the foreground. The horizontal stripes have to go.

The new faults are in craft. The pen is a glossy toy-blue cylinder; make it a satin or matte barrel with a metal clip and a cyan tip, and give it a firm contact shadow where it crosses the slip. The three brass tabs sit on a thin rod and read as a UI slider. Make them separate cast-brass tabs set into or resting on the slab, each with its own contact shadow and bevel. Keep the count at three with the second one lit, but light it with a warm glint, not a flat pale yellow fill.

Earlier fix 1 landed only in part. The carts now sit back to back at the centre and the paired cyan reads at once, but the split is still a thin rod with a faint pane. There is no 3 cm glazed partition, no sill, no top rail, and the two glows dont reflect in it. Build the partition as a real glass panel with a visible thickness edge catching the key, an aluminium sill and head rail running to the back wall, one diagonal reflection streak, and a soft cyan mirror of each screen on the glass.

Earlier fix 2 mostly landed. New fault: a flat empty beige band runs from under the front wall to the footer, about a sixth of the frame, and the floor is a flat blue sheet. Lower the cutaway so its front wall base meets the footer wash, or give the plinth a cut caliche face with strata and a soft indigo contact shadow. Give the floor vinyl seams and a faint sheen under the casters.

Take the desk out of the type band: pull it back and right so its front edge stops above the headline top line, or crop it hard at the right edge; the type wash leaves a seam through the lower right third. Turn the page over with one corner lifted toward camera so it reads plainly as face down. Keep the stethoscope coil whole inside the frame.

Finish the people where the eye lands: the clinicians raised hand is a soft kit fist holding a white clump; make it an open hand, palm toward the actor. Give the actor a held pose, one hand on her knee, shoulders squared toward him, gown folds and a contact crease on the table paper, both casting indigo contact shadows.

Round 1 fix 1 partly landed: the objects still cover about an eighth of the frame, not a third, and are primitives. Bring the camera closer and lower so the pair fills about a third; model each laptop with rounded corners, a radiused lid edge, a hinge barrel with a lid seam and rubber feet with tight contact shadows; rebuild the stethoscope with a Y binaural, eartips, a rimmed chest piece and matte tubing coiling loosely with contact shadows.

Round 1 fix 2 landed. New fault: the front desk top is a smeared out of focus texture with a dark blurred halo under the laptops, reading as a compositing patch. Give the desk crisp grain in focus, let the sun bars fall across it, and replace the halo with physical contact shadows matching the window key.

Fix 1 mostly landed. The pointer did not land as a clear read: the carriage is a big gold block with a knob and a small orange sliver. Slim it into a knurled slider sitting on the rail with a bevelled brass needle dropping onto the first ridge beside a short engraved zero ridge, so stands at zero reads at 432 px.

Fix 2 partly landed. The slab front face is blocky low resolution blotching reading as tan wood or sponge. Swap in a high resolution pale limestone with fine fossil pitting and a softly chipped rounded front arris, carry the indigo shadow under the rail and tabs into that face, and give the indigo end cap a brushed anodised finish with a small chamfer catching the key.

Fix 1 partly landed. The tilt is still shallow; at 432 px it reads as a flat cyan block in a window. Increase the paddle angle, run the specular along the curve, cast a harder longer indigo shadow from the proud lip across the steel.
Fix 2 mostly landed. The board grain is still a fine even horizontal streak; widen to soft irregular grain bands with knots or a cathedral figure varied board to board. No other new fault.

Round 1 fix 1 mostly landed. New fault: the right boards top rail runs into the last dek line. Drop both boards about 80 to 100 px or trim one hook row of board above the top row so the dek clears the rail by a full line height.

Round 1 fix 2 landed only in part: the lean reads about 10 to 15 degrees. Swing the camera harder so the near column comes up about 1.4 times the far column; thicken the tubing with a clear specular, show the hook pins standing out with the coils hanging on them, chest pieces as discs with thickness and a chrome rim. Keep the blue channel.

Round 1 fix 1 partly landed: the rolls render as blue glass cylinders and both sheets lie dead flat with no crinkle, curl, drape or contact shadow, so they still read as chart bars. Make the rolls matte off white paper with a wound edge, a crinkle normal map, a 2 to 3 cm lift and curl at each free end with an indigo contact shadow; scale the stethoscope and glove box to true size.

Round 1 fix 2 partly landed: the hand rests palm down instead of pinching the corner; pose it pinching with the sheet ramping up to the fingers; give the counter a hard contact shadow; drop the camera and push in about 20 percent so the far sheet and the clinician rise into the empty peach band.

Connect the receiving side to the tool: run the three rails to a cyan glowing laptop, or put a cyan lit receiving pan on the far edge in line with all three rails so each empty pan sits at the tools end. Drop the camera to about seated eye height behind the clinicians shoulder, closer in, so the three stations recede toward that glow.

Crop or pose the kit hands so no hand reads at feed size; curled stacked paper with contact shadows under each shuttle; a bevelled limestone top with edge wear and colour instead of a grey slab; brass or turned feet on the legs.

Round 2 fix 2 did not land: the slab front face is streaky horizontally smeared lavender and peach bands reading as a stretched texture; replace with a correctly UV mapped high resolution limestone face with fossil pitting, a softly chipped arris and indigo shadow down the face; the end cap is still a flat box, give it a chamfer and brushed anodised grain.

Round 2 fix 1 only partly landed: the needle is an unreadable sliver at 432 px and the carriage still a full width block; shrink to a slim slider with a bevelled brass needle pointing straight down onto one taller engraved zero ridge that catches a highlight.

The glass wall is still the weakest thing: replace the rod with a 12 mm full height glass panel with a lit cyan white thickness edge, a brushed aluminium sill and a head rail into the rear wall, one diagonal reflection streak and a soft low opacity mirrored cyan ghost of each monitor; kill the white bloom flare at the monitors.
Break up the flat blue floor with sheet vinyl seams toward the camera, a faint sheen picking up the cyan screens and tighter indigo contact shadows under every caster and shoe.

Earlier fix 1 mostly landed but the page is a small white sliver at 432 px; bring the desk forward and left into the open floor right of the headline with a sheet at least 0.30 m on screen, plainly face down with a faint print bleed, one corner curled and casting its own shadow, and a single unused faint cyan tool glow beside it.

Earlier fix 2 half landed: the clinicians raised hand is still a soft kit mitt and both bodies read as mannequins; lower or hide the hand, add gown folds, a crease and dip in the table paper under her, soft indigo contact shadows under both pairs of shoes and the stool casters.

Seat the laptop stack on the sweep: a crisp contact shadow under the bottom laptops feet instead of an offset indigo blob, a rear hinge barrel, rubber feet, a lid seam and radiused lip, and two separate equal cyan sleep dots that do not merge.
Tighten the binder shadow to a contact hardening shadow, let the floor take a faint reflection or gradient, show the tangerine bookcloth weave and worn turned corners.
Fix 1 partly landed: the right rail sits about 40 px below the last dek line, under one line height; lower the right board about 25 px or the camera slightly.

Fix 2 partly landed: lean about 1.15 to 1.25; hook pins should stand about 3 cm out with each coil over a pin and a shadow gap behind; chest pieces about twice the diameter with a bright chrome rim; bring the near board closer so the near column is about 1.4 times the far.

Make the paper and tables look real: head rolls as cylinders with cardboard cores in chrome brackets, crepe crinkle under a low raking key, a visible 3 to 4 cm curl at each free end with its own shadow, bevelled cabinets with a toe kick, drawer seams and pulls, a stainless step with a rubber tread instead of black slabs.

Set both tables parallel and drop the camera to fill the dead peach strip under the source pill; move the year pills off the vinyl onto the sweep or cabinet face; remove or scale up the tiny stethoscope.

The laptop fix half landed: sleep lights blur at 432 px, the stack still hovers with no visible hinge or feet and an offset cast shadow; seat it with a tight contact line, model a hinge barrel and feet, make each light a crisp cyan pill on the front lip.

The binder fix did not land: the bookcloth shows only as a thin rim and the binder sits in a soft halo; show a band of woven cloth with corner wear and replace the halo with a short contact shadow and one directional cast.
The glass panel landed; the one ghost is a lone cyan shard mid air between the carts, take it out or replace it with a real low opacity reflection of both monitors on the pane.
The floor fix partly landed: contact shadows are tight, but the floors are flat swatches with no seams or sheen; lay vinyl seams, a soft specular streak and a faint cove.
The needle only half landed: engrave a raised brass zero ridge twice the graduation height at the stop with the pointer seated hard against it and one shared contact shadow.
The limestone landed; the end cap still faces camera square on as a flat elevation, swing the camera about 15 degrees and cut the empty limestone front band to about half.
The slab still reads as sand fading into a haze band; bring a chamfered chipped limestone lip into the lower third with fossil pitting and end the back at a real edge.
The pen still reads as glossy plastic; a satin anodised barrel with a knurled grip lying flat with a tight contact shadow; slips with curl and a hairline contact shadow.
The clinicians hands are still two mannequin fists above the bench edge mid frame; rest the forearms flat or put a hand on the ask shuttle with a contact shadow, or crop them.
The bench is still a plain pale grey slab on tube legs; dressed limestone with a chamfered edge, slab thickness, warm albedo with tooling, a skirt or trestle base.

Model the tables as real exam tables with recessed kick bases, set in drawers, stirrup brackets and a head roll on a dispenser bar; replace the wavy vinyl noise with a stitched seam and sheen; make the tables truly parallel.
Give the paper thickness, a visible roll and a 2 to 3 cm curl at the free end with a shadow and a crinkle normal map; move the year pills off the vinyl onto the sweep.
